element_id_on_error_screen.question: Does showing raw elementId (e.g. "timer_esc_1") in the violation context line violate the anti-UUID discipline?
element_id_on_error_screen.verdict: No — not the same class of problem, judged acceptable as-is
element_id_on_error_screen.reasoning: The anti-uuid gate (and the doctrine behind it) targets DATABASE-BACKED entity/actor identifiers shown to a user with no way to resolve them to a human-meaningful name (e.g. a raw actor UUID instead of a person's name via an actor-resolver). elementId here is a BPMN diagram-element id AUTHORED BY THE SAME PERSON currently looking at the SAME open diagram in the SAME editor — it is the canvas's own addressing scheme (analogous to a cell reference in a spreadsheet formula error, or a line number in a compiler error), not an opaque foreign-system key. There is no resolver that could turn it into something more 'human' than what the modeler itself assigned. It was ALSO already present pre-fix (buried unreadably inside the truncated JSON blob — JSON.stringify({type,elementId,elementKind,message}) puts elementId right after type), so this is strictly a presentation improvement, not a new exposure.
element_id_on_error_screen.non_blocking_followup: elementKind (e.g. "boundaryEvent", "userTask") is shown verbatim in raw BPMN camelCase — English technical vocabulary embedded mid-sentence in an otherwise Russian title line. Same pre-existing-content caveat applies (it was already in the pre-fix truncated JSON), but now that it has visual prominence next to a translated title, the English/Russian mix reads more noticeably. Cheap, symmetric follow-up: a small ELEMENT_KIND_LABELS map (same pattern as VIOLATION_TYPE_LABELS, ~7 known kinds) would close this. Not blocking — the current state is still a strict readability win over the pre-fix truncated JSON, and elementKind's role here is identification, not the primary message.

message_body_language_note.observation: The .message body itself (the part now shown IN FULL) is raw English text with embedded XML syntax (e.g. '<boundaryEvent id="timer_esc_1"> is a NON-INTERRUPTING boundary timer (cancelActivity="false")...'), authored server-side in src/core/bpmn-linter.ts. T-0659's Russian layer is the TITLE + structural framing only — the task's own goal statement ('человеческим русским') is only partially delivered: the CATEGORY is Russian, the DETAIL text is English/XML-technical.
message_body_language_note.in_scope_or_not: Out of scope for T-0659 as correctly scoped by the builder — the server contract (LintViolation.message strings) was explicitly and verifiably untouched (confirmed: zero diff under src/). Translating or humanizing the message bodies would require a server-side change and is a materially different task.
message_body_language_note.verdict: non-blocking, real, worth a follow-up ticket — but net strictly better than the pre-fix state (previously ~12 garbled characters of this same English text were visible; now the whole thing, including the actionable 'Fix:' clause, is readable by anyone comfortable with technical English, e.g. support staff escalating to a developer). Approving T-0659 does not require closing this gap.
